package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"maps"

	"example.com/fixture/internal/runtime"
)

// Each function below reads a guarded key in a shape the gate must not treat as modeled.

// compared: a comparison is not a nil check.
func compared(cfg *runtime.Config) bool {
	return cfg.Extra["nodes"].(map[string]interface{})["allow_remote"] == true
}

func tbl(m map[string]interface{}, k string) map[string]interface{} {
	t, _ := m[k].(map[string]interface{})
	return t
}

// throughHelper indexes a helper call's result directly.
func throughHelper(cfg *runtime.Config) interface{} {
	return tbl(cfg.Extra, "nodes")["allow_remote"]
}

// packageLiteral is a func literal outside any function declaration.
var packageLiteral = func(cfg *runtime.Config) interface{} {
	return cfg.Extra["nodes"].(map[string]interface{})["tier"]
}

// marshaled hands the section to encoding/json, which the Extract also calls.
func marshaled(cfg *runtime.Config) []byte {
	b, _ := json.Marshal(cfg.Extra["nodes"])
	return b
}

// localName names the section through a local holding a constant.
func localName(cfg *runtime.Config) interface{} {
	sec := "nodes"
	return cfg.Extra[sec]
}

func countKeys(v interface{}) int { m, _ := v.(map[string]interface{}); return len(m) }

// parentTable hands the whole [agents] table to a helper no family registers.
func parentTable(cfg *runtime.Config) int {
	return countKeys(cfg.Extra["agents"])
}

// aliasRange ranges over the tree through a local.
func aliasRange(cfg *runtime.Config) int {
	x, n := cfg.Extra, 0
	for range x {
		n++
	}
	return n
}

// marshaledTree hands the whole tree to encoding/json.
func marshaledTree(cfg *runtime.Config) []byte {
	b, _ := json.Marshal(cfg.Extra)
	return b
}

// rangedAll ranges over the tree through a stdlib iterator.
func rangedAll(cfg *runtime.Config) bool {
	for k, v := range maps.All(cfg.Extra) {
		if k == "nodes" {
			b, _ := v.(map[string]interface{})["allow_remote"].(bool)
			return b
		}
	}
	return false
}

// The tree laundered through a module wrapper that marshals or ranges it.
func dumpTree(m map[string]interface{}) []byte { b, _ := json.Marshal(m); return b }

func wrappedDump(cfg *runtime.Config) []byte { return dumpTree(cfg.Extra) }

func countTree(m map[string]interface{}) (n int) {
	for range m {
		n++
	}
	return n
}

func wrappedRange(cfg *runtime.Config) int { return countTree(cfg.Extra) }

func passN(n int) int { return n }

// nestedStdlib hands the tree to a stdlib call wrapped in a module one.
func nestedStdlib(cfg *runtime.Config) int { return passN(len(maps.Collect(maps.All(cfg.Extra)))) }

// sameLine hides an unsafe use behind a safe one on the same line.
func sameLine(cfg *runtime.Config) ([]byte, error) {
	return json.Marshal(map[string]interface{}{"all": cfg.Extra, "has": cfg.Extra["x"] != nil})
}

// computedKey names the section at run time.
func computedKey(cfg *runtime.Config, s string) interface{} { return cfg.Extra[s] }

// dumpSection looks like a section helper but marshals the whole tree.
func dumpSection(m map[string]interface{}, name string) []byte { b, _ := json.Marshal(m); return b }

func viaHelper(cfg *runtime.Config) []byte { return dumpSection(cfg.Extra, "nodes") }

type box struct{}

func (box) pick(leak, safe map[string]interface{}) []byte {
	_ = safe["x"]
	b, _ := json.Marshal(leak)
	return b
}

// methodExpr passes the tree as the method's first parameter (argument 1).
func methodExpr(cfg *runtime.Config) []byte { return box.pick(box{}, cfg.Extra, nil) }

// rangeKey and pointerKey rewrite a key local after its constant start.
func rangeKey(cfg *runtime.Config) (v interface{}) {
	k := "x"
	for _, k = range []string{"nodes"} {
	}
	return cfg.Extra[k]
}

func pointerKey(cfg *runtime.Config) interface{} {
	k := "x"
	p := &k
	*p = "nodes"
	return cfg.Extra[k]
}
